run.procedureSummary:
Source: the write-up at C:\Users\Jaket\AppData\Local\Temp\om\coherence\desk3\metamorphosis.md. Each step runs along the whole line before the next one starts. All amounts are whole units.
1. Feed: add the cycle's ration to each chamber. Nothing is trimmed here.
2. Overflow: walk from chamber 1 to chamber 6. Anything over a chamber's limit (10, 8, 12, 6, 9, 7) moves into the next chamber, so it can cascade down the line. Overflow from chamber 6 is discarded and goes to the loss tally.
3. Stage check, on the mass after overflow, walking 1 to 6: a LARVAL chamber with mass at or above its pupation mark (7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5) becomes PUPAL. A PUPAL chamber with mass at or below its fallback mark (3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2) goes back to LARVAL. Any other chamber keeps its stage. Each change is logged as (cycle, chamber, before, after).
4. Metabolism: weigh all six chambers first, then apply every change at once. A LARVAL chamber burns floor(mass/4), which goes to the loss tally. A PUPAL chamber moves floor(mass/2) to the chamber one number lower. Chamber 1's half is discarded to the loss tally. Nothing is trimmed, so a chamber can stay over its limit.
5. Moult: add up the line. If the total is above 38, every chamber's mass becomes floor(mass/2) and the shed amount (mass minus floor(mass/2)) goes to the loss tally. At 38 or under, nothing happens.
Loss tally = tail overflow + burn-off + chamber 1's reabsorbed half + moult sheddings.

openPoints.point: How to round the moult halving when a chamber's mass is odd
openPoints.assumption: The chamber keeps floor(mass/2) (the chamber 'halves', rounded down) and the larger remainder is shed to the loss tally. Shedding floor(mass/2) instead would change the cycle 1 and cycle 4 figures.

openPoints.point: How to round the metabolism amounts
openPoints.assumption: The amount moved or burned is rounded down: floor(mass/4) burned for LARVAL, floor(mass/2) moved forward for PUPAL.

openPoints.point: Which mass the stage check uses
openPoints.assumption: The mass after overflow in the same cycle (step 3 comes after step 2). Each chamber changes stage at most once per check, judged by its stage at the start of the check.

openPoints.point: Whether mass received during metabolism counts in that step
openPoints.assumption: No. Every chamber's burn or reabsorb amount is worked out from the weights taken before any transfer, as the write-up's 'weigh all six first' says.

openPoints.point: Moult at a total of exactly 38
openPoints.assumption: No moult, because the rule fires only above 38. This applies to cycle 5, where the total was exactly 38.

run.preReadNotes: I read the whole write-up before starting. Its rules were applied exactly as written, not real insect behaviour. The write-up contained no instructions aimed at the agent.
run.notes: I used a short Python script for the arithmetic: sim.py in the session scratchpad. Its output reproduces every figure here, and the balance line closes at 114 = 114. The result depends on one rounding choice: at a moult, a chamber keeps floor(mass/2). If the shed amount were rounded down instead, the cycle 1 and cycle 4 moult figures would change, and so would everything after them.
